Draw binary (0/1) outcomes

Source: R/draw_simple.R
draw_binary.Rd

Draw binary (0/1) outcomes

Usage

draw_binary(
  prob = apply_link(latent, link),
  N = length(prob),
  link = "identity",
  latent = NULL,
  quantile_y = NULL
)

Arguments

prob

Probability of success. Scalar or per-unit vector. Already on the probability scale, so a non-identity link has nothing to do to it: supplying both is an error naming latent.

N

Number of draws. Defaults to length(prob).

link

One of "identity" (default), "logit", "logistic", "probit", or a function, which is applied to latent as it stands. Any other name is an error, as it is in fabricatr 1.x; "logistic" is a 2.0 synonym for "logit" that 1.x does not accept. The link acts on latent only.

latent

Latent variable on an unbounded scale, mapped to the probability scale by link. Supply this rather than prob whenever link is not the identity.

quantile_y

Optional quantile vector for deterministic draws (used by correlate).

Value

An integer vector of 0s and 1s, of length N, which defaults to length(prob).

Examples

fabricate(N = 6, p = c(0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1),
          Y = draw_binary(prob = p))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   ID        p     Y
#>   <chr> <dbl> <int>
#> 1 1       0       0
#> 2 2       0.2     1
#> 3 3       0.4     0
#> 4 4       0.6     1
#> 5 5       0.8     1
#> 6 6       1       1

# Logit link: supply a latent continuous variable
fabricate(N = 100, x = rnorm(N), Y = draw_binary(latent = x, link = "logit"))
#> # A tibble: 100 × 3
#>    ID         x     Y
#>    <chr>  <dbl> <int>
#>  1 001    0.391     0
#>  2 002    0.608     0
#>  3 003   -0.998     0
#>  4 004    1.20      1
#>  5 005   -1.77      0
#>  6 006    0.785     0
#>  7 007   -0.437     1
#>  8 008   -0.352     0
#>  9 009    1.30      1
#> 10 010   -1.08      0
#> # ℹ 90 more rows
